items.headline: USCIS announces second random selection for FY2027 H-1B cap
items.summary: USCIS conducted a second random selection from previously submitted FY2027 H-1B registrations to reach the annual cap. Selected registrants may file cap-subject petitions during the stated 90-day window. No additional registration fee is required for the second round.

items.headline: Practitioners report uptick in H-1B specialty-occupation RFEs this cap season
items.summary: Corporate immigration attorneys report an increase in Requests for Evidence challenging the specialty-occupation basis of FY2027 cap-subject H-1B petitions. The RFEs commonly ask for detailed degree-to-role connections and beneficiary qualifications.

items.headline: USCIS updates Policy Manual guidance on EB-2 National Interest Waiver evidence
items.summary: USCIS revised its Policy Manual section on EB-2 NIW adjudications, clarifying how officers weigh an applicant's proposed endeavor and its national importance. Practitioners note the update may shift RFE patterns for petitions filed after the effective date.

items.headline: Analysis: EB-3 backlog dynamics and what they mean for skilled workers
items.summary: A commentary piece analyzes recent EB-3 priority-date movement and the structural drivers of the skilled-worker backlog. The article is analysis, not a government announcement, and draws on published Visa Bulletin history.

items.headline: DHS publishes final rule adjusting Form I-140 and I-907 filing fees
items.summary: DHS published a final rule in the Federal Register adjusting several USCIS filing fees, including Form I-140 (immigrant petition) and Form I-907 (premium processing), effective 60 days from publication. The rule affects employment-based petition costs across EB-1, EB-2, and EB-3.
